comments.author: @HiddenCanada
comments.text:
Canada has some incredible places hiding in plain sight, and the Smoking Hills might be one of the strangest! 🔥

A big thank you to everyone who's been suggesting places for us to investigate. I really appreciate your support!

If there's another mysterious place in Canada you'd like me to explore, leave it below. Your suggestion might become our next documentary!

And if you enjoyed this one, please give it a like and subscribe to Hidden Canada!

comments.author: @onyourwing5696
comments.text:
Not a scientist, nor an investigator... Just a curious layman.
Can't they locate the slump's offshore leading edge and/or earliest/deepest deposits from drilled core samples...
Then date how long the transition from burnt/unburnt material has been exposed to saltwater immersion?

replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: That’s an interesting approach. A dated offshore layer containing burnt material could show that burning had already happened by then. The tricky part is separating when the rock burned from when it slid into the sea, saltwater exposure alone wouldn’t give a straightforward date. I haven’t found a study testing that approach here, but it’s a thoughtful question.
